reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its normed additive commutative group and Borel measurable structures, all x,y in E and real tau,q satisfying tau>0 and q>1, define G(a) as the pushforward of canonical centered standard Gaussian under z to a+sqrt(tau)z, and L(z)=exp(inner(x-y,z-y)/tau-norm(x-y)^2/(2tau)). Then L is measurable; G(x)=G(y).withDensity(ofReal L); G(x) is absolutely continuous with respect to G(y); and the extended nonnegative RN derivative dG(x)/dG(y) equals ofReal L G(y)-almost everywhere. The real-valued function z to (ENNReal.toReal(dG(x)/dG(y)(z)))^q is integrable under G(y), meaning almost-everywhere strongly measurable with finite integral of its norm. Its real Bochner integral is exactly exp(q(q-1)norm(x-y)^2/(2tau)). Real.log of that same integral divided by q-1 equals q norm(x-y)^2/(2tau). Powers with q are real powers. ENNReal.toReal is the real conversion, including its totalized value at infinity; the integral and logarithm involve the actual RN derivative, not a separately postulated likelihood. The integration and a.e. reference measure are both G(y). Dimension zero is included. There is no restriction on x,y, no upper bound on q or additional parameter assumption. The G,L definitions scope over the full conjunction. Constants 2,q-1,q(q-1) are exactly those displayed, with no unspecified or existential constants.
